title: Initial severity and antidepressant benefits: a meta-analysis of data submitted to the Food and Drug Administration
authors: Kirsch I, Deacon BJ, Huedo-Medina TB, Scoboria A, Moore TJ, Johnson BT
population: 35 placebo-controlled trials of fluoxetine, venlafaxine, nefazodone and paroxetine from FDA medical and statistical reviews obtained under the Freedom of Information Act; sertraline and citalopram reviews were also obtained but lacked complete data
funder: The authors received no specific funding for this study.
authorConflicts: IK has received consulting fees from Squibb and Pfizer; the other authors declared no competing interests.
result: Weighted mean improvement 9.60 points on the Hamilton scale with drug and 7.80 with placebo, a difference of 1.80, below the 3-point NICE criterion; the difference reached that criterion only at mean baseline scores of about 28. For sertraline, four trials with 486 participants, 38% of patients in sertraline trials, were reported by the FDA as not achieving a significant drug effect without mean scores. Three sertraline trials allowed replacement of patients not improving after 2 weeks, and trials excluded patients who improved by 20% or more during a 1- to 2-week placebo washout.
